title: staging-velocity-map-gpu-fleet-tiling-and-burst-schedule-q4-2026
summary: Working sheet: phasewise GPU fleet staging and utilization projections across North America, Europe, and APAC. This doc maps a staggered launch plan with warm pools, burst windows, and operational guardrails for Q3–Q4 2026. Purpose: give infra/product/finance enough visibility to sign off capacity commits and optional burst credits.
assumptions: 1) Baseline request growth = +38% q/q across hosted API users. 2) We prioritize latency-sensitive traffic to NA, then EU, then APAC (latency routing policy A). 3) Fleet mix initially: 60% A100-80GB, 30% A100-40GB, 10% H100 reserved for high-throughput customers. 4) Warm GPU pool target = 12% of deployed GPUs for each region. 5) Spot/cheap capacity lever limited in EU due to procurement constraints.
capacity_by_region:
ASCII table:
Region | Mar-2026 | Jun-2026 | Sep-2026 | Dec-2026 | Target utilization (baseline)
NA     | 1,200 GPUs | 1,650 GPUs | 2,100 GPUs | 2,400 GPUs | 62%
EU     | 480 GPUs  |  720 GPUs  | 1,020 GPUs | 1,320 GPUs | 58%
APAC   | 240 GPUs  |  360 GPUs  |  540 GPUs  |  780 GPUs  | 55%
Notes: counts are logical GPU equivalents after bin-packing and quantization gains. Warm pool and burst buffer included in totals. Reserve lanes: 5% of NA fleet assigned to enterprise SLA lanes.
rollout_timeline:
Milestones:
- 2026-03-01: Finalize vendor quotes and reserve A100-80GB order windows (NA primary).
- 2026-04-10: Spin up first warm pool in NA (150 GPUs) and enable canary routing for latency-sensitive routes.
- 2026-05-15: EU pilot (50 GPUs warm pool) + deploy cross-region fallback routing.
- 2026-07-01: APAC soft launch with burst lanes on cloud provider X (initial 100 GPUs via reserved + spot mix).
- 2026-08-15: Autoscale policy rollout: sustained-utilization triggers and pre-warm triggers enabled.
- 2026-10-01: Full regional ramp to target fleet counts; begin deprecating older 40GB-only nodes where quantized models are validated.
- 2026-11-20: Post-ramp runbook review and capacity headroom audit.
Dependencies: hardware delivery windows, finance commit approvals (by 2026-04-01), licensing for private customers.
surge_strategy:
Burst windows and throttles:
- Planned surge windows tied to marketing events (Black Friday type sim) will be pre-scheduled; we maintain a 20% burst credit in NA and EU, 15% in APAC.
- Burst mechanics: preference to spin temporary cloud-burst nodes in same region, fallback to cross-region only under SLA-level degradation.
- Throttle rules: per-customer throttles when sustained queue latency > 250ms and regional util > 85%.
- Cost mitigation: pre-warm cheaper quantized variants for low-priority routes and switch during surge to preserve latency for premium routes.
operational_plan:
Runbook excerpts and owners:
- Oncall rotations: infra-capacity-pager (Evan/Priya week-of); escalate to SRE lead if cross-region fallback triggered > 2x in 24h.
- Telemetry: per-model per-route QPS, p50/p95 latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate reported every 5m to Console dashboards.
- Canary & rollback: automated canary switches after onboarding 50 GPUs per region for 48h with synthetic load. Rollback threshold: >5% increase in token latency or >3% model degradation on eval prompts.
- Finance ops: hourly burn alerts if spot/ondemand mix deviates >10% from forecast.
- Tickets: JIRA INFRA-1284 = EU pre-warm; JIRA INFRA-1299 = NA enterprise lanes config.
risk_and_mitigations:
Top risks:
1) Hardware ship delays -> mitigation: overnight spot-burst contracts and contingency with alternate vendor; maintain 8-week buffer in procurement calendar.
2) Unexpected cross-region latency spikes during fallback -> mitigation: tighten routing policy thresholds, increase KV cache replication for hot prefixes, and add synthetic health checks.
3) Cost overruns during surges -> mitigation: enforce burst budget with auto-shutdown after 6h unless approved by finance; prefer quantized run to cut token cost.
4) Regulatory/blocking in APAC regions -> mitigation: staged private-deploy path and local compliance checklist; use dedicated capacity for regulated customers.
